neighbours.label: contexts setting up a comparison or contest among several items (often confused, one another, four-way)
fire: affect, effect Often confused words. Affect is usually a verb.
complement, compliment Sometimes confused nouns with different meanings.
The sixty-four teams play one another to decide the champion.
The election became a four-way battle between the major parties.
These churches are as different from each other as Baptists, Lutherans and Methodists.
principal, principle Often confused or misspelled in essays.
The five clubs compete against one another every spring.
It turned into a three-way race among the candidates.
quiet: affect Usually a verb. It means to influence something.
complement A noun meaning something that completes another thing.
The team plays at home to decide the champion.
The election became a quiet affair for the major party.
This church has its own traditions and practices.
principal The head of a school, written in essays.
The club trains on the field every spring.
It turned into a long race for the candidate.
